title: Expiring for Love is Beautiful But Stupid Wooden Postcard
dimensions: 10 x 15 cm (Printed Matter lists 15 x 10 cm; the card is landscape)

description.main: A one-line Truism by Jenny Holzer, printed in red capitals on a thin wooden postcard and issued as a multiple by Printed Matter, New York. The text comes from Truisms (1977-79), the alphabetised statements Holzer first pasted up anonymously around downtown Manhattan.
description.extended:
A one-line Truism by Jenny Holzer, printed in red capitals on a thin wooden postcard and issued as a multiple by Printed Matter, New York.

The sentence comes from Truisms (1977-79), more than 250 single-line statements written to sound like proverbs. Holzer wrote them as a student in the Whitney Independent Study Program, set them in alphabetical order on anonymous posters and pasted them up around downtown Manhattan. In April 1979 they filled the windows of Printed Matter's storefront on Lispenard Street, and they have since appeared on T-shirts, LED signs and stone benches. This card is digitally printed and belongs to a set of sixteen wooden postcards drawn from Truisms and Survival (1983-85), issued in red, black, gold and silver text.

Holzer (born 1950) turned from painting to language at the Rhode Island School of Design in the mid-1970s. She received the Golden Lion at the 1990 Venice Biennale as the first woman to represent the United States, and Printed Matter has shown and sold her work since the late 1970s.

notes: Red text variant [Red Text]; Printed Matter's wooden postcard series runs to sixteen texts from Truisms and Survival, issued in red, black, gold and silver text variants (this title was found only in red). Text from the Truisms series (1977-79). Publisher: Printed Matter Inc. / J. Holzer, New York; process listed as Digital; Printed Matter stock 112342. Year not given on the Printed Matter record; dealers date the edition 2018 (Twelve Books, eBay) or 2020 (FairArt), and a dealer listing names the wood as cherry. Printed Matter lists 15 x 10 cm; the product photo shows the card in landscape orientation. An earlier balsa-wood postcard of the same text was published by Fotofolio, New York (after 1994). Acquired from Printed Matter, New York: https://www.printedmatter.org/catalog/14295. Not signed.
